candidates.title: Two cases of gigantism with divergent long-term outcomes: the impact of genetics and treatment adherence.
candidates.abstract: Gigantism is a rare disorder caused by growth hormone excess before epiphyseal closure. Long-term follow-up data are limited, particularly regarding the influence of genetic background and treatment adherence on disease outcomes. We report two adolescents diagnosed with gigantism during puberty who were followed at a tertiary endocrinology center for 12 and 21 years, respectively. Diagnosis was established based on elevated insulin-like growth factor 1 levels, failure of growth hormone suppression during oral glucose tolerance testing, and pituitary magnetic resonance imaging findings. Case l,a 14-year-old female, presented with accelerated linear growth, whereas Case 2, a 14-year-old male, was diagnosed following an orthopedic complication. Both patients had pituitary macroadenomas and underwent transsphenoidal surgery followed by treatment with somatostatin analogs. Germline genetic analysis of the AIP and MEN1 genes was performed using Sanger sequencing of coding exons and flanking regions from DNA extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes. One patient achieved sustained biochemical and structural remission after surgery and long-term somatostatin analog therapy, leading to treatment discontinuation. The other patient exhibited poor treatment adherence, persistent hormonal hypersecretion, residual tumor, and progressive systemic complications. Genetic analysis identified a pathogenic germline AIP nonsense variant (c.804C>A; p.Tyr268*) in the patient with unfavorable clinical evolution, whereas no pathogenic variants were detected in the other case. These findings illustrate divergent clinical trajectories in gigantism and highlight the combined impact of genetic background and treatment adherence on long-term outcomes, supporting the importance of genetic evaluation and sustained follow-up in early-onset disease.

candidates.title: Impact of inhibitors on treatment patterns and disease burden in Chinese patients with hemophilia: a cross-sectional study.
candidates.abstract: Systematic investigations on the impact of inhibitors on treatment modalities and overall disease burden in Chinese hemophilia patients based on real-world data remain limited. We analyzed a cross-sectional survey of 543 patients diagnosed with hemophilia in China as of 31 December 2022. Treatment, bleeding, and cost items used recall periods specified in the questionnaire. Group comparisons were descriptive and exploratory. The mean age of participants was 26.0 ± 14.8 years, with 99.63% being male. The inhibitor-positive group had a higher proportion of severe hemophilia (93.64% vs. 76.56%, p < 0.001). 54.88% of the patients had disability certificates, and the proportion increased with age. Nearly 90% of the patients older than 30 years had different degrees of disability. The median annual bleeding rate was 20 (IQR 8-36) episodes in inhibitor-positive patients versus 12 (IQR 3-30) in inhibitor-negative patients (p = 0.008). The mean annual prophylaxis infusion frequency was 127.71 ± 54.11 infusions per year (approximately 2.5 infusions per week; median 120, IQR 96-168), with a mean factor consumption per infusion of 21.16 ± 8.28 IU/kg. The average annual per-patient cost was CNY 520,415 ± 773,627, of which the cost of factor therapy was CNY 279,402 ± 627,427. In this selected survey sample, inhibitor-positive patients reported a higher median number of bleeding episodes and greater treatment complexity.

candidates.title: Iatrogenic Cushing Syndrome With Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis Suppression in a Two-Month-Old Infant Following Unsupervised Topical Corticosteroid Use: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Topical corticosteroids are commonly prescribed in pediatric dermatology; however, systemic adverse effects may occur rapidly in infants due to increased percutaneous absorption, the occlusive effect of diapers, and the immaturity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. We report the case of a two-month-old, 6 kg male infant who developed iatrogenic Cushing syndrome following approximately seven weeks of daily and repeated unsupervised application of a betamethasone valerate 0.1% topical corticosteroid to the diaper area for the treatment of diaper rash. Clinical examination revealed moon facies, a buffalo hump, and facio-truncal obesity. Laboratory evaluation showed suppressed morning cortisol at 5 µg/L (reference: 50-230 µg/L) and undetectable adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) at 2.47 pg/mL (reference: 7-63 pg/mL), consistent with secondary adrenal insufficiency due to HPA axis suppression; brain CT showed no structural abnormality of clinical relevance. Management consisted of gradual withdrawal of the topical corticosteroid over four weeks, physiologic hydrocortisone replacement therapy at 8-10 mg/m²/day in three divided doses, and close clinical and biochemical follow-up. Biochemical recovery was suggested by normalization of morning cortisol to 272 µg/L, allowing progressive tapering and the discontinuation of hydrocortisone over six weeks without any episode of acute adrenal insufficiency. The family received structured education regarding the risks of unsupervised corticosteroid use and the warning signs of adrenal crisis. This case underscores that even moderate-to-potent topical corticosteroids applied to occluded skin areas can cause significant systemic toxicity in this vulnerable population and highlights the critical importance of parental education, appropriate prescribing guidance, and vigilant monitoring to prevent this avoidable complication.

candidates.title: Structural brain abnormality, pharmacotherapy, and treatment resistant schizophrenia management: a systematic review and critical appraisal.
candidates.abstract: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) affects up to 30% of patients with schizophrenia and carries a substantial burden, yet clozapine, the only antipsychotic specifically indicated, is delayed by years because resistance is recognized retrospectively. Neuroimaging may provide objective biomarkers to shorten this delay. We searched PubMed and Scopus to June 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. We included peer-reviewed neuroimaging studies investigating TRS, covering structural, functional, and metabolic modalities; studies not addressing TRS were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies and RoB 2 for randomized trials. Findings were synthesized qualitatively, without meta-analysis. Of 1502 identified records, 1179 were screened and 94 studies were included (44 structural, 18 functional, and 32 metabolic). TRS was characterized by extensive abnormalities in frontal cortical, limbic, and white matter pathways and, compared with treatment-responsive schizophrenia (nTRS), by the absence of striatal dopaminergic hyperactivity, alongside functional and metabolic alterations in frontal and cortico-subcortical circuits. Evidence concerning ultra-treatment-resistant schizophrenia (uTRS) remains scarce. Neuroimaging findings support a distributed cortico-subcortical phenotype and a non-dopaminergic, potentially glutamatergic pathophysiology in TRS. However, the evidence remains constrained by small, heterogeneous, predominantly cross-sectional studies, with uTRS still poorly investigated. PROSPERO (CRD420261437825).

candidates.title: Protective Effects of Quercetin and Eugenol on Auditory Dysfunction Associated With Oxidative Stress in a Type 2 Diabetic Rat Model.
candidates.abstract: To assess oxidative stress-associated auditory dysfunction in a streptozotocin-nicotinamide (STZ-NA)-induced type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) rat model and to determine the protective effects of the phenolic compounds eugenol and quercetin. T2DM was induced in Sprague-Dawley rats using STZ-NA. Beginning 21 days after induction, eugenol or quercetin was administered for 28 consecutive days. Oxidative stress was assessed by measuring serum malondialdehyde (MDA) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) levels using ELISA. Auditory function was evaluated using auditory brainstem responses (ABR), elicited by click and tone-burst stimuli at 8, 16, 24, and 32 kHz. ABR thresholds were elevated in T2DM animals across all frequencies, with the greatest impairment observed at 24-32 kHz. Serum MDA levels increased and SOD levels decreased in T2DM, whereas both interventions partially restored redox balance (p < 0.05). At 32 kHz, ABR thresholds correlated positively with MDA and negatively with SOD, with MDA identified as an independent predictor. The STZ-NA-induced T2DM rat model exhibits frequency-dependent auditory impairment and delayed neural conduction associated with oxidative stress. Eugenol and quercetin confer functional otoprotective effects, and high-frequency ABR measurements may serve as indicators for early detection and monitoring of diabetes-related auditory dysfunction.
candidates.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

candidates.title: Neuronavigation-assisted versus conventional endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary adenomas: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
candidates.abstract: Evidence on the benefit of intraoperative neuronavigation in endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal (EET) pituitary surgery remains mixed. We conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing navigation-assisted and conventional EET surgery for pituitary adenomas, to estimate the effect size for a definitive multicentre trial. At Ain Shams University (April 2025-February 2026), 57 patients with pituitary adenomas were assessed for eligibility; 7 were excluded for prior Gamma Knife radiosurgery. The remaining 50 were randomized 1:1 within strata of tumor size, functional status, and surgery status, with concealed computer-generated allocation. Recruitment continued until the planned 25 patients per arm were enrolled. The primary outcome was extent of resection; secondary outcomes included operative time, blood loss, visual and hormonal outcomes, and complications. All 50 patients (25 per arm) were analyzed by intention-to-treat. Gross total resection was numerically higher with navigation (28.0% vs. 16.0%; p = 0.496); adjusted for Knosp grade, the odds ratio was 2.66 (95% CI 0.41-17.06) versus a crude 2.04. Extent of resection was strongly associated with tumor size, functioning status, and Knosp grade; no giant adenoma achieved gross total resection. Blood loss was lower with navigation (median 250 vs. 350 mL; p = 0.016), with no difference in operative time, which included navigation setup (p = 0.788). Neuronavigation did not significantly improve extent of resection, though resection completeness trended favorably with navigation across most subgroups. The associated blood-loss reduction remains hypothesis-generating. A definitive, adequately powered multicentre trial is warranted. Pan African Clinical Trial Registry, PACTR202608562462156, registered retrospectively on 17 August 2026.

candidates.title: Multiple co-occurring genetic variants in an elderly patient with Liddle's-like syndrome: a case report and literature review.
candidates.abstract: Liddle syndrome (LS) is a rare autosomal dominant condition classically defined by early-onset hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and a suppressed renin-aldosterone profile, primarily driven by gain-of-function mutations in the SCNN1A, SCNN1B, or SCNN1G genes encoding the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC). Nevertheless, genetically investigated cases exhibiting Liddle's-like phenotypes in the elderly population remain exceptionally rare. We report a 61-year-old male admitted with recurrent limb weakness and resistant hypertension. A comprehensive clinical workup, including biochemical profiles, RAAS evaluation, and 24-h ABPM, was conducted to exclude common secondary causes. Following informed consent, whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed, with candidate variants validated by Sanger sequencing and assessed per ACMG/AMP guidelines. To guide therapeutic management, a narrative literature review of similar cases was also performed searching PubMed, Web of Science, and CNKI using keywords like "Liddle syndrome," "elderly," "hypertension," and "hypokalemia.". Admission tests showed hypokalemia (2.94 mmol/L), compensated metabolic alkalosis, and suppressed renin-aldosterone levels. 24-h ABPM indicated severe blood pressure fluctuations up to 185/120 mmHg. Genetic testing revealed three heterozygous variants of uncertain significance (VUS)-CYP3A5 (c.1253 + 83C > T), SCNN1G (c.1727A > G, p.Lys576Arg), and WNK1 (c.5636A > T, p.Asp1879Val)-without any known pathogenic variants. A diagnostic trial with triamterene (50 mg twice daily) restored normal potassium levels (> 3.5 mmol/L). After a 30-day combination therapy of controlled-release nifedipine and irbesartan, blood pressure stabilized between 110 and 133 and 69-85 mmHg. We report an elderly patient with chronic hypokalemia and resistant hypertension. After ruling out common secondary causes (for example, primary aldosteronism, Cushing's syndrome, pheochromocytoma), Liddle's-like syndrome was clinically diagnosed based on the low-renin/low-aldosterone biochemical phenotype, compensated metabolic alkalosis, literature review, and a selective response to triamterene. This case suggests that Liddle's-like syndrome must be considered in the differential diagnosis of hypokalemic hypertension in older adults to ensure early and targeted therapy.

candidates.title: Clinical Presentation and Targeted Genetic Evaluation of Familial Isolated Pituitary Adenomas: A Single-Center Case Series.
candidates.abstract: Background: Familial isolated pituitary adenomas (FIPA) are characterized by considerable clinical and genetic heterogeneity. Although germline pathogenic variants in AIP account for a subset of cases, most FIPA families remain genetically unexplained. We aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, tumor phenotype, treatment outcomes, and targeted genetic evaluation of FIPA families from a tertiary endocrine referral center. Methods: We retrospectively identified FIPA families among patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) evaluated at a tertiary endocrine referral center between 2019 and 2024. FIPA was defined as PitNETs occurring in at least two related individuals without clinical features suggestive of syndromic endocrine disease. Clinical, radiological, histopathological, and genetic data were analyzed. Results: Among 1068 patients with PitNETs, seven FIPA families were retrospectively identified (0.66% of the source cohort), comprising 20 affected individuals. Index cases included four women and three men, with a mean age at diagnosis of 37.1 ± 17.3 years. Somatotroph PitNETs predominated among index cases (5/7), whereas nonfunctioning PitNETs were more frequent among affected relatives (9/13). Six of seven index tumors were macroadenomas, and cavernous sinus invasion was present in two. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in AIP or MEN1 were identified by Sanger sequencing, and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) detected no copy number alterations involving AIP, MEN1, or CDKN1B. Conclusions: This series highlights the clinical heterogeneity of FIPA and the differing tumor spectrum between index cases and affected relatives. The absence of pathogenic variants identified by targeted genetic testing further illustrates the genetic heterogeneity of familial pituitary tumor predisposition.

candidates.title: Fight or Flight: A Multidisciplinary Approach to Diagnosis and Management of Mediastinal Paragangliomas.
candidates.abstract: Mediastinal paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors, leading to potentially invasive clinical investigation and inadequate staging. Functional secretory activity, high germline mutation rates, multifocal disease burden, and proximity to the great vessels demand a multidisciplinary approach. We describe our longitudinal multidisciplinary experience building a center of excellence model. We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of 19 patients with mediastinal paraganglioma managed at a quaternary referral center, capturing demographics, imaging, preoperative testing, operative details, and perioperative outcomes. There were 14 (73.7%) females with a median age of 46.3 years (IQR 38.5-57.6 years). Sixteen (84%) of 19 patients were referred from outside centers; 9 (47.3%) underwent biopsy before referral, with three (15.8%) experiencing catecholamine crisis, pneumothorax, or hemorrhage. Nine (47.4%) tumors were adjacent to the aorta, and seven (42.1%) adjacent to the pulmonary artery, with vascular involvement in 17(89.5%) of the 19 patients. Thirteen (68%) were functional and five (26.3%) had multifocal disease. Succinate dehydrogenase mutations were found in 63.6% of patients tested. Cardiopulmonary bypass was required in 63.2%, with zero 30-day mortality. Postoperative complications occurred in 47.4%, predominantly atrial arrhythmia. Median hospital stay was four days. Four patients developed local recurrence at a median recurrence-free survival of 16.9 months, all with positive margins or multifocal disease. Mediastinal paragangliomas can be safely resected within a multidisciplinary center of excellence. Early recognition, avoidance of uninformed biopsy, functional staging, preoperative alpha blockade, and tumor profiling and genetic evaluation with genetic counseling are essential components.

candidates.title: The unseen risk: a systematic review of the incidence, management, and outcomes of the trigeminocardiac reflex in skull-base surgery.
candidates.abstract: This study synthesizes contemporary evidence on the trigeminocardiac reflex (TCR) during skull-base and adjacent neurosurgical procedures, with emphasis on operative corridors, triggers, hemodynamic phenotypes, management, and the limits of current outcome evidence. Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase through September 15, 2024. Eligible reports described intraoperative TCR or closely related trigeminal autonomic responses during skull-base surgery or adjacent procedures and reported event features, management, or outcomes. Twenty-eight studies including 329 patients met inclusion criteria. Reported TCR events clustered in microvascular decompression for trigeminal neuralgia (n=168; 51.1%), CPA/posterior fossa or anterior skull-base tumor surgery (n=71; 21.6%), transsphenoidal pituitary procedures (n=47; 14.3%), and percutaneous trigeminal procedures (n=35; 10.6%). Immediate cessation of the provoking maneuver was the cornerstone of management, with anticholinergics, vasoactive agents, or temporary pacing required only in selected severe or recurrent cases. No TCR-attributable mortality was reported. However, evidence regarding long-term functional outcomes remains limited, inconsistently reported, and largely dependent on historical vestibular schwannoma and pituitary cohorts. A procedure-specific synthesis identifies high-risk maneuvers, preventive considerations, and escalation options for each operative corridor. TCR should be anticipated during trigeminal manipulation across skull-base surgical corridors and managed initially by immediate cessation or modification of the provoking stimulus, with pharmacologic or resuscitative escalation reserved for persistent or severe events. Although the available evidence supports a procedure-specific approach to prevention and preparedness, heterogeneous definitions, retrospective designs, and incomplete denominators preclude reliable incidence estimates or validated management recommendations.

candidates.title: Diagnostic challenge of delayed immune-related hepatitis during zongertinib treatment after nivolumab plus ipilimumab in a 52-year-old man with HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Delayed immune-related hepatitis after discontinuation of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is increasingly recognized, but attribution is difficult when liver injury develops during subsequent tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This diagnostic dilemma has not been well described during human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-selective TKI treatment after dual ICI therapy. A 52-year-old Japanese man with HER2 exon 20 insertion-positive stage IVB non-small cell lung cancer received nivolumab plus ipilimumab from February 28 to November 13, 2025, and developed grade 2 oral mucositis, grade 2 adrenal insufficiency, and grade 1-2 skin toxicity. Zongertinib was initiated on November 26. Routine testing on January 6, 2026 showed grade 3 hepatocellular injury, and zongertinib was withheld. Despite drug withdrawal, liver injury progressed, and he was admitted with mild fatigue on January 20, when aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and γ-glutamyl transpeptidase levels were 774, 1,386, 156, and 160 U/L, respectively. Total bilirubin remained approximately 1.0 mg/dL. Viral and autoimmune testing and imaging disclosed no alternative cause. Liver biopsy showed active hepatitis with lymphocyte-predominant portal and lobular inflammation and interface activity, findings compatible with an immune-mediated hepatitis pattern but not specific for the causative agent. Prednisolone 40 mg/day (approximately 0.5 mg/kg/day) produced rapid biochemical improvement with resolution of fatigue. Zongertinib was resumed on February 11 and continued without recurrent hepatitis through June 2026. The progression of liver injury despite zongertinib withdrawal, multiple prior immune-related adverse events, exclusion of competing causes, compatible histology, corticosteroid responsiveness, and absence of recurrence after zongertinib rechallenge collectively favored delayed immune-related hepatitis, although zongertinib-associated drug-induced liver injury could not be completely excluded. In similar cases, a structured etiological assessment, including liver biopsy when the result may alter cancer treatment, can help guide management.

candidates.title: Hemodynamic Challenges After Paraganglioma Resection in Fontan-Palliated Adult With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
candidates.abstract: Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease is associated with increased risk of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), particularly among patients with single-ventricle physiology. A 26-year-old man with unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect and extracardiac Fontan palliation, and Fontan-associated liver disease presented with hypertensive crisis, with imaging evidence of PPGL. The patient underwent robotic right adrenalectomy and nodule resection complicated by high-volume chylous ascites for several weeks. Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease, particularly univentricular physiology, is a well-established driver of PPGL. Existing guidelines mandate preoperative α-blockade and volume expansion for functional PPGL, but this approach is not tailored to Fontan physiology. We present a rare case of operative disruption of retroperitoneal lymphatics superimposed on Fontan-associated systemic venous and lymphatic congestion. Right heart catheterization, cautious α-blockade with volume expansion, and multidisciplinary perioperative management are essential to balance catecholamine blockade against the risks of venous congestion, lymphatic failure, bleeding, and thrombosis.

candidates.title: When Thyrotropin Meets Growth Hormone: The Clinical Challenges of a Mixed GH/TSH-Secreting PIT1-Lineage Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumour.
candidates.abstract: Background: Acromegaly is most commonly caused by a growth hormone (GH)-secreting pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (PitNET). Plurihormonal PIT1-lineage PitNETs are uncommon, and combined GH and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) secretion poses distinctive diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report a mixed GH/TSH-secreting PIT1-lineage PitNET in which the biochemical response to preoperative lanreotide supported the clinical suspicion of a functionally relevant thyrotroph component before targeted pathological reassessment. Case Presentation: A 39-year-old woman presented with a two-year history of progressive acral enlargement, headaches, hyperhidrosis, snoring, and voice deepening. Biochemical evaluation showed IGF-1 1128 ng/mL (reference range 93.1-281), GH 61 µg/L, TSH 1.5 µIU/mL (0.35-4.94), FT4 1.66 ng/dL (0.7-1.5), and FT3 7.0 pg/mL (1.8-4.2). Pituitary MRI demonstrated a 15 × 14 × 10.5 mm macroadenoma. Lanreotide 120 mg every four weeks reduced IGF-1 to 846 ng/mL and GH to 14 µg/L while normalizing FT4 (1.04 ng/dL) and FT3 (3.9 pg/mL), reinforcing the suspicion of mixed GH/TSH secretion. Transsphenoidal surgery was performed in October 2024. The tumour was initially classified as a densely granulated somatotroph PitNET; prompted by the preoperative biochemical phenotype, additional β-TSH immunostaining demonstrated positivity in numerous tumour cells, leading to reclassification as a mature plurihormonal PIT1-lineage PitNET (Ki-67 approximately 1%). Postoperative biochemical remission was not achieved, and MRI demonstrated a 7 mm residual lesion. Lanreotide was resumed, with the sustained control of the thyrotroph component but persistent GH/IGF-1 excess. Because residual disease persisted with slight cavernous sinus extension, Gamma Knife radiosurgery was performed in July 2026. Conclusions: Mixed GH/TSH-secreting PIT1-lineage PitNETs may be overlooked when TSH is inappropriately normal rather than frankly elevated. This case illustrates the value of integrating biochemical findings, treatment response, and targeted histopathological reassessment. Persistent disease despite surgery and somatostatin receptor ligand therapy further highlights the frequent need for multimodal, long-term management.

candidates.title: When hypertensive crisis mimics septic shock: A case report of pheochromocytoma-induced severe lactic acidosis following GLP-1 receptor agonist administration.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a rare catecholamine-secreting tumor that may present atypically with severe lactic acidosis and systemic inflammatory features, closely mimicking sepsis and delaying diagnosis. A possible interaction with glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists has been suggested but remains poorly understood. A 48-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with acute nausea, vomiting, chills, severe abdominal pain, and hypertensive crisis within hours of self-administering tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist. She was febrile, tachycardic, and markedly hypertensive, with severe lactic acidosis and systemic inflammatory markers suggestive of sepsis. Initial evaluation favored sepsis; however, negative cultures, sustained severe hypertension, hyperlactatemia disproportionate to perfusion status, and elevated urinary normetanephrines redirected the evaluation toward an endocrine cause. The clinical and biochemical picture supported a diagnosis of probable pheochromocytoma. Imaging revealed a fat-containing left adrenal mass initially suggestive of myelolipoma, representing a diagnostic pitfall. The patient was managed with intravenous fluids, a continuous nicardipine infusion, and oral alpha-blockade with doxazosin. Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics were started and later discontinued as infection became unlikely. Beta-blockade was withheld until adequate alpha-blockade was achieved. Supportive care and electrolyte correction were provided. Blood pressure and lactate improved over 48 hours with clinical stabilization. The patient was discharged on oral alpha-blockade with plans for outpatient functional imaging (64Cu-DOTATATE positron emission tomography) and definitive surgical evaluation. Pheochromocytoma should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained lactic acidosis and hypertensive crisis, even when sepsis appears likely. Catecholamine-driven type B lactic acidosis can closely mimic infectious shock. Fat-containing adrenal lesions do not exclude pheochromocytoma, and biopsy should be avoided. The temporal association with GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure is hypothesis-generating and warrants further investigation as use of these agents continues to expand.

candidates.title: Sildenafil as an Emerging Analgesic: Mechanistic Insights and Therapeutic Potential in Pain Management.
candidates.abstract: Neuropathic pain is pain resulting from damage or disease affecting the peripheral or central nervous system. Chronic neuropathic pain is a major clinical concern and is frequently unresponsive to standard analgesics, so multimodal treatments have been suggested. There is substantial evidence supporting a role for the nitric oxide (NO)/cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) signaling pathway in nociceptive processing. It is unclear what the specific function of phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE-5) in the NO/cGMP pathway is in response to pain. In the present review, we aimed to evaluate potential peripheral interactions of sildenafil, a PDE-5 inhibitor. Sildenafil is a specific and strong inhibitor of phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE-5). The enzyme PDE-5 primarily degrades cGMP, an intracellular second messenger. Inhibition of cGMP breakdown results in higher intracellular cGMP concentrations, which are considered largely responsible for its therapeutic effect. This is a lacuna in the present literature, and this study seeks to provide an overall overview of the therapeutic potential of sildenafil in pain management. This realization of sildenafil's broader potential may lead to new therapeutic opportunities, the optimization of current strategies, and the expansion of its clinical use.
candidates.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

candidates.title: Non-diabetic endocrine neuropathies: A practical approach to diagnosis and clinical evaluation.
candidates.abstract: Peripheral neuropathy has diverse etiologies, with endocrine disorders beyond diabetes representing significant, yet frequently underrecognized causes. While diabetic neuropathy is well established, this article specifically excludes a detailed discussion of diabetic neuropathy to focus on less-recognized endocrine causes and presents a practical diagnostic algorithm for their earlier and more accurate identification. A focused narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus and ScienceDirect (2015-2025). From 2,318 screened records, 154 studies were included after full-text review of 298 articles. Evidence was synthesized by etiology, mechanism, clinical presentation and diagnostic relevance. Disorders such as hypothyroidism, acromegaly, adrenal dysfunction and deficiencies of vitamins B12 and D produce distinct neuropathic profiles via metabolic, hormonal, inflammatory or compressive mechanisms. Subclinical nerve involvement is common, with electrophysiological abnormalities detectable in up to 60% of asymptomatic individuals. Characteristic clinical patterns - such as delayed reflexes in hypothyroidism, bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) in acromegaly and sensory ataxia in B12 deficiency - provide diagnostic clues. Based on synthesized evidence, a stepwise diagnostic algorithm was developed to guide clinical evaluation. Endocrine disorders are important and often reversible causes of peripheral neuropathy. Early recognition requires a systematic approach. The proposed evidence-based algorithm offers clinicians a practical tool to improve diagnostic efficiency, facilitate timely treatment of the underlying endocrine condition and reduce the risk of irreversible nerve damage.

candidates.title: Subarachnoid Pneumocephalus Following Endoscopic Transsphenoidal Surgery.
candidates.abstract: A 26-year-old man with past medical history of prolactinoma presented two weeks status post endoscopic transsphenoid prolactinoma excision with a positional headache and cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea; he was found to have diffuse subarachnoid air. There are few reports of subarachnoid pneumocephalus in the emergency medicine literature. Pneumocephalus, particularly tension pneumocephalus, typically occurs in the setting of traumatic skull fractures. However, emergency physicians should be aware of subarachnoid pneumocephalus in the setting of endoscopic skull base surgeries.
candidates.journal: Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine

candidates.title: Geometry-Driven Biomechanical Optimization of Double-J Ureteral Stents.
candidates.abstract: Ureteric stents are widely used to maintain ureteric patency; however, complications such as stent migration, ureteric irritation, and patient discomfort remain common. Although several geometric parameters of double-J stents have been investigated in relation to urinary flow, stenosis, reflux, encrustation, stent length, and coil characteristics, the specific biomechanical role of terminal coil orientation relative to physiological loading remains insufficiently characterized. This study proposes a geometry-based biomechanical framework that considers terminal coil-plane orientation as a specific and mechanistically insufficiently characterized geometric variable in double-J ureteral stent stability. The framework integrates biomechanical principles, engineering concepts, and clinical considerations to provide a simplified mechanistic interpretation of how coil geometry may interact with multidirectional physiological loading generated by ureteral peristalsis and intravesical pressure. Changes in coil-plane orientation may alter the transmission and decomposition of physiological forces, potentially influencing axial loading, transverse forces, bending response, stent-wall contact, and resistance to longitudinal displacement. An alternative terminal coil-plane orientation is proposed as a testable geometric modification that may alter these mechanical relationships without changing the overall dimensions or material composition of the device. The proposed relationships are conceptual and do not represent validated stress distributions, experimentally demonstrated retention benefits, or evidence that any particular coil orientation is superior. This framework provides a structured basis for future finite element analysis, computational fluid dynamics, and fluid-structure interaction studies, followed by experimental and clinical validation, to quantitatively evaluate coil orientation as a complementary geometric variable in double-J ureteral stent design and development.

candidates.title: Endogenous hypercortisolism and cardio-liver-metabolic dysfunctions: from pathogenesis to the effects of therapeutic strategies targeting hypercortisolism.
candidates.abstract: Endogenous hypercortisolism, namely Cushing's syndrome (CS) is a rare but severe endocrine disorder caused by chronic exposure to excess glucocorticoids and characterized by substantial morbidity and increased mortality. Persistent hypercortisolism profoundly affects multiple cardiovascular and metabolic pathways, leading to a broad spectrum of cardio-liver-metabolic complications including arterial hypertension, cardiac and vascular remodelling, thrombotic diathesis, hepatic steatosis, visceral obesity, impaired glucose metabolism, and dyslipidemia. These alterations arise from complex interactions between direct glucocorticoid effects on target tissues and indirect mechanisms, mainly involving insulin resistance, endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and altered lipid metabolism. The primary therapeutic objective in CS is the normalization of cortisol excess through surgery, radiotherapy, or medical therapy, namely pharmacological treatment. In recent years, the availability of medical drugs targeting pituitary ACTH secretion, adrenal steroidogenesis, or glucocorticoid receptor signalling has expanded therapeutic options for patients with CS, especially with persistent or recurrent disease. Beyond biochemical control of hypercortisolism, namely normalization of urinary free cortisol (UFC) (UFC ≤ upper limit of normal), accumulating evidence suggests that these treatments may improve several cardiometabolic manifestations associated with cortisol excess. However, although remission of hypercortisolism leads to significant clinical improvement, complete normalization of cardio-liver-metabolic alterations is not consistently achieved. Many patients continue to exhibit persistent cardiovascular and metabolic abnormalities even after long-term biochemical remission, highlighting the need for active long-term monitoring and multidisciplinary management to prevent disease progression and optimize long-term outcomes. This mini-review briefly outlines the pathogenesis of cardio-liver-metabolic dysfunctions and discusses the potential effects of currently available therapeutic strategies targeting hypercortisolism on these comorbidities.

candidates.title: Trigeminal autonomic cephalgia due to pituitary adenomas: scoping review of the literature.
candidates.abstract: Trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias (TAC) are a debilitating subtype of headaches and have been associated with pituitary adenomas. Treatment of associated pituitary adenomas has been reported to result in resolution of the secondary TACs, although this association is poorly understood. We conducted a scoping review of the literature in accordance with PRISMA guidelines using Medline, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. We identified all relevant cases to detail the epidemiology, clinical phenotype of TACs, characteristics of the associated pituitary lesion including its hormonal profile, type of clinical intervention, and outcomes. 57 cases were included in the final review. Most patients had secreting adenomas (91%). Short-lasting Unilateral Neuralgiform headache attacks with Conjunctival injection and Tearing (SUNCT) and Probable SUNCT were the most common TAC phenotype diagnosed (47%), followed closely by cluster headaches/ and cluster-like headaches (46%). Medical intervention was attempted in every patient with an average of 4.8 trials of medications attempted before headache relief. 98% of patients had either complete resolution or improvement of headaches associated with treatment (medical or surgical). 26 patients underwent surgery, of which 18 (69%) had either improvement or complete resolution of headaches. Patients with TACs secondary to pituitary adenomas are likely to be diagnosed with SUNCT, have associated secreting adenomas, and to underwent multiple trials of medications before reaching headache relief. In the included cases, TACs secondary to prolactinomas had improvement associated with medical management with dopamine agonist therapy. Surgical resection of pituitary adenomas in patients with medically refractory TACs and growth-secreting adenomas was also associated with significant improvement in headache severity. Further work is required to understand the exact pathophysiological mechanism for this rare disease in order to better treat this rare condition moving forward.

candidates.title: Anoikis in Gastric Cancer: Mechanistic Insights Into Metastatic Survival and Therapeutic Targeting.
candidates.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely because many patients present with advanced or metastatic disease. Anoikis, a specialized form of detachment-induced apoptosis, is a critical safeguard that eliminates epithelial cells after loss of appropriate extracellular matrix (ECM) and cell-cell adhesion; therefore, its disruption allows malignant cells to survive outside their native niche and acquire metastatic competence. In GC, anoikis resistance is central to tumor progression and peritoneal dissemination, enabling detached tumor cells to survive anchorage loss, mechanical stress, metabolic adaptation, and immune pressure before colonization. This review synthesizes current evidence on how anoikis is initiated, executed, and evaded in GC. Mechanistically, anoikis initiation begins with disruption of integrin-ECM and cadherin-mediated adhesion, followed by focal adhesion remodeling, cytoskeletal reorganization, and suppression or rewiring of adhesion-dependent survival signaling. Anoikis execution converges on mitochondrial and death-receptor apoptotic pathways, including Bcl-2 family regulation, caspase-8/caspase-9 activation, and executioner caspase cleavage. In contrast, anoikis evasion is driven by interconnected survival hubs, including integrin/FAK/Src, PI3K-AKT, MEK-ERK, NF-κB, Wnt/β-catenin, YAP/TEAD, BDNF/TrkB, and protective autophagy. GC-specific mediators such as TCF7L2/PLAUR, MYH9/CTNNB1, ITGBL1/AKT/FBLN2, CAV1/epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)/ITGB1, GRP94/YAP-TEAD1, GDF15/autophagy, and TRIM69/PRKCD/BDNF further illustrate how detached GC cells acquire metastatic survival capacity. Translationally, these pathways provide a rationale for biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring anoikis sensitivity or disabling compensatory survival programs. Targeting anoikis resistance may therefore complement existing chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy approaches, particularly in GC subtypes characterized by peritoneal dissemination, EMT, YAP/TEAD activation, or integrin/PI3K-AKT pathway dependence.
candidates.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

candidates.title: Adherence to hormone replacement and associated factors in patients with hypopituitarism.
candidates.abstract: To evaluate adherence to hormone replacement therapy and identify factors associated with nonadherence in patients with hypopituitarism. This cross-sectional study included 126 adults with hypopituitarism followed at a tertiary neuroendocrinology center in Brazil. Adherence was assessed using the Morisky-Green Test (MGT), which was translated, culturally adapted, and validated for the Brazilian context in patients with hypopituitarism, and by the modified Brief Medication Questionnaire (BMQ). Association between clinical, socioeconomic, and treatment-related variables were analyzed. Good adherence was observed in only 28% and 27% of patients according to the MGT and BMQ, respectively, with moderate or low adherence predominating. Polypharmacy was common (61.1%) and was associated with lower adherence. In multivariate analysis, female sex (odds ratio [OR] = 2.78,95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.14-6.82), use of psychotropic medications (OR = 3.23, 95% CI = 1.08-9.63), a higher number of medications (OR = 1.26 per additional drug, 95% CI = 1.03-1.55), and absence of glucocorticoid replacement (OR = 3.31, 95% CI = 1.16-9.44) were independently associated with nonadherence. No associations were found for age, education level, income, duration of hypopituitarism, etiology, metabolic syndrome, or healthcare access variables. Adherence to hormone replacement therapy in hypopituitarism remains suboptimal and is negatively associated with female sex, polypharmacy, and psychotropic medication use. These findings suggest the need for further evaluation of patient-centered strategies, education, and regimen simplification to improve long-term adherence.

candidates.title: Long-term disease control in Knosp grade 4 Cushing's disease using maximal safe resection and early adjuvant radiotherapy.
candidates.abstract: Knosp grade 4 Cushing's disease (CD) represents an anatomically extreme and clinically challenging subtype of pituitary neuroendocrine tumor because a lesion extending deeply lateral to the intracavernous internal carotid artery (ICA) is rarely amenable to complete and safe resection via transsphenoidal surgery. Persistent hypercortisolism in CD directly compromises long-term survival, while aggressive lateral cavernous sinus (CS) dissection carries substantial neurovascular risk. Dedicated outcome studies focusing exclusively on Knosp grade 4 CD remain scarce. Therefore, the authors evaluated the long-term outcomes of a treatment strategy combining maximal safe resection with early adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) for residual CS disease while intentionally avoiding excessively aggressive lateral CS dissection beyond the ICA. The authors retrospectively reviewed the records of consecutive patients with biochemically confirmed CD and Knosp grade 4 CS invasion treated between 2009 and 2025. The surgical strategy prioritized maximal safe tumor resection while avoiding excessively aggressive dissection lateral to the ICA. Early adjuvant stereotactic RT was administered for residual lateral CS disease. Clinical, endocrinological, and radiological outcomes were analyzed during long-term follow-up, and factors potentially associated with poor disease control were explored. Thirty patients were included in the analysis. Endocrinological and radiological disease control was achieved in 26 (87%) of them during a mean follow-up of 70.5 months. Tumor progression occurred in 4 patients, all of whom demonstrated persistent hypercortisolism, and 3 subsequently died of disease-related causes. Prior RT exposure and an elevated Ki-67 labeling index were associated with poorer disease control despite multimodal treatment including temozolomide. In contrast, durable endocrine control was achieved in all Crooke cell adenoma cases under the described treatment strategy. No patient experienced ICA injury or disabling cranial neuropathy attributable to aggressive lateral CS dissection. For Knosp grade 4 CD, durable endocrine control must be balanced against the risks of radical CS surgery. Maximal safe resection combined with early adjuvant RT for residual CS disease provided favorable long-term disease control while avoiding major surgical morbidity. These findings support planned early adjuvant RT as a reasonable strategy for residual lateral CS disease in this rare and anatomically extreme subtype.

candidates.title: Beware of Tall Stature: Growth Hormone Excess Associated with a Rare Parasellar Extra-Axial Tumour-Diagnostic and Management Challenges in a Resource-Limited Setting.
candidates.abstract: Tall stature can be the sole indicator of growth hormone (GH) excess, which causes pituitary gigantism before epiphyseal fusion. In developing regions like Indonesia, a lack of systematic screening often delays diagnosis. While classic presentations involve accelerated linear growth, atypical cases may be dominated by neurological signs, such as seizures secondary to tumour mass effect. A 14-year-old boy presented with a 2-year history of rapidly accelerating growth velocity, increasing shoe size, and a 6-month history of severe morning headaches accompanied by drug-resistant focal seizures. Endocrine evaluations revealed significantly elevated basal GH (4.27 ng/ml) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels (536 ng/ml). Brain magnetic resonance imaging identified a large parasellar extra-axial tumour with suprasellar extension. The patient underwent a craniotomy and tumour excision; histopathology subsequently confirmed a rare, aggressive malignant mesenchymal tumour. Postoperatively, the patient achieved seizure resolution and normalization of GH and IGF-1 levels. However, he developed evolving pituitary dysfunction consistent with multiple pituitary hormone deficiency (MPHD), specifically central hypothyroidism, necessitating targeted hormonal replacement therapy and continuous clinical follow-up. GH excess and gigantism can arise secondary to parasellar pathology rather than intrinsic pituitary disease, with neurological features like refractory epilepsy occasionally preceding classic endocrine manifestations. Rapid adolescent growth paired with neurological signs warrants urgent structural neuroimaging. Meticulous perioperative pituitary monitoring and early multidisciplinary involvement are essential to optimize long-term patient outcomes. Pituitary gigantism can be driven by extra-axial parasellar masses rather than intrinsic pituitary adenomas, operating via mass-effect compression that disrupts hypothalamic somatostatin inhibition.Drug-resistant epilepsy and severe headaches caused by local tumour infiltration can dominate the clinical picture, meaning rapid adolescent growth paired with neurological symptoms mandates urgent magnetic resonance imaging of the brain.Postoperative multiple pituitary hormone deficiency often evolves silently over weeks or months, requiring lifelong, multidisciplinary surveillance to detect late-stage deficiencies like secondary adrenal insufficiency.
candidates.journal: European journal of case reports in internal medicine

candidates.title: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) is a rare congenital disorder characterized by an interrupted or absent pituitary stalk, ectopic posterior pituitary, and anterior pituitary hypoplasia, resulting in varying degrees of hypopituitarism. An 18-year-old white American male with a history of panhypopituitarism, adrenal insufficiency, and Asperger's syndrome presented with seizures. Examination revealed short stature and absent secondary sexual characteristics. Endocrine evaluation demonstrated multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a hypoplastic anterior pituitary gland, ectopic posterior pituitary, and absent pituitary stalk, confirming the diagnosis of PSIS. Hormone replacement therapy with hydrocortisone, levothyroxine, growth hormone, and testosterone enanthate was initiated. PSIS should be considered in patients with growth failure, delayed puberty, and multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies. Early recognition and timely hormone replacement are critical to optimize growth, pubertal development, and long-term outcomes.

candidates.title: Adrenal ganglioneuroma in an adolescent presenting as an incidentaloma: Imaging-pathology correlation and diagnostic challenges: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal ganglioneuroma (AGN) is a rare, benign, and usually nonfunctioning tumor arising from neural crest-derived sympathetic ganglion cells. Preoperative diagnosis is difficult because the clinical presentation is often nonspecific, and imaging findings overlap with those of other adrenal neoplasms. We describe an adolescent adrenal incidentaloma with detailed imaging-pathology correlation, adding to the small number of reported adolescent cases. A previously healthy 16-year-old male underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) after a bicycle accident. No traumatic injury was identified, but imaging incidentally revealed a well-circumscribed right adrenal mass measuring approximately 6.1 cm × 3.6 cm × 5.0 cm. CT and magnetic resonance imaging showed progressive, persistent enhancement across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases without demonstrable washout (attenuation increased from 20 Hounsfield units unenhanced to 55 Hounsfield units in the venous phase, with further qualitative enhancement on 15-minute delayed images) and no intralesional fat, suggesting a non-adenomatous lesion and raising suspicion for a neurogenic tumor. Biochemical evaluation showed no evidence of hormonal hypersecretion. Histopathological examination after resection established the diagnosis of AGN. The patient underwent right adrenalectomy because of the size and radiologically indeterminate nature of the mass. The postoperative course was uneventful. Transient elevation of blood pressure noted during follow-up prompted biochemical reevaluation, which showed no evidence of excess catecholamine. Follow-up CT at 9 months showed no recurrence. Progressive delayed enhancement without washout and absence of signal loss on opposed-phase magnetic resonance imaging, a pattern previously described in ganglioneuroma, may suggest the diagnosis preoperatively, although definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation. Complete surgical excision established the diagnosis and achieved a favorable short-term outcome; the excellent long-term prognosis of AGN is supported by the published literature, and our patient remains recurrence-free at 9 months.

candidates.title: Photocatalytic Disruption of Concurrent Redox Axes Elicits Convergent Redox Collapse.
candidates.abstract: The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual-inhibitor regimens is hampered by pharmacokinetic asynchrony. Herein, we report squaraine-based photocatalysts as a single-agent modality that concurrently disrupts these interconnected antioxidant systems in cancer cells. Upon 635 nm light irradiation, IITC depletes intracellular NADPH and GSH through photocatalytic oxidation coupled with type I/II photosensitization. NADPH depletion deprives the reductive coenzyme of thioredoxin reductase in the thioredoxin axis, while glutathione oxidation collapses the central antioxidant axis. Consequently, IITC ablates both antioxidant axes concurrently and exerts potent phototherapeutic anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, during phototherapy IITC undergoes self-immolation into nontoxic degraded fragments, thereby avoiding phototoxicity post-treatment. This self-eliminating, metabolism-targeted photocatalytic strategy establishes a new avenue for safe and efficient cancer phototherapy.

candidates.title: Reirradiation for Recurrent Craniopharyngioma-Long-Term Follow-up.
candidates.abstract: To report long-term tumor control, toxicity, and functional outcomes after a second course of fractionated radiation therapy for recurrent craniopharyngioma previously treated with radiation therapy. We identified all patients with craniopharyngioma with recurrent or progressive disease, unsuitable for further medical management or re-resection, who underwent 2 courses of fractionated photon radiation therapy at a single institution between 1998 and 2024. Reirradiation was delivered to 54 Gy in 30 fractions with full overlap of the initial target; dose constraints to optic nerves, chiasm, and brainstem were Dmax/D0.03cc (Maximum Dose or Dose to 0.03 cubic centimetres) ≤54 Gy. Outcomes were summarized descriptively. Six patients received reirradiation a mean of 9.8 years (range, 5.6-20.5) after initial radiation therapy (50-54 Gy in 25-30 fractions). Median follow-up after reirradiation was 4.1 years (range, 0.4-8.8). At the last follow-up, 4 patients were alive, all with local disease control (2 with radiological regression, 2 with stable disease). Two deaths occurred (1 due to progressive disease and 1 due to functional decline with stable imaging). Visual outcomes were heterogeneous: 1 patient maintained intact vision; others had intermittent diplopia, bitemporal hemianopsia, or unilateral blindness with contralateral impairment. Endocrinopathy was frequent: 3 of 4 survivors had pan-hypopituitarism; 1 had partial deficits (hypothyroidism/amenorrhea). Functional status was impaired in survivors, with the inability to work or study due to fatigue, visual loss, or cognitive issues. Additional toxicities included posttreatment seizures requiring hospitalization (n = 1) and transient dexamethasone for headache (n = 1). In carefully selected patients lacking other curative options, modern highly conformal reirradiation can achieve meaningful local control after prior high-dose radiation therapy, but carries an additive risk of visual, endocrine, and functional morbidity. Decisions should be individualized within a multidisciplinary team to identify appropriate cases for reirradiation and to ensure thorough long-term follow-up to manage delayed toxicity.
